sheets.prompt:
Four-panel character reference sheet following the reference layout: three full-body views (front / side / back) left to right, and one large head-and-shoulders close-up filling the right column; the exact same character, outfit and proportions in every panel; plain background. The first reference image is only the panel layout guide: copy its four-panel arrangement, not its grey mannequin shapes. Panel 1 (left): full-body front view, standing in a stately neutral pose, showing the card-panel front of the robe. Panel 2: full-body true side profile, showing how flat the rectangular robe panel is. Panel 3: full-body back view showing the card-back pattern of the robe panel. Panel 4 (tall right column): head-and-shoulders close-up with the crown, facing the camera, neutral expression, face clearly lit. Each full-body figure is drawn a little small inside its panel, complete from the top of the crown to the soles of the shoes with clear space above and below, standing on a small patch of plain floor with a soft contact shadow; if any part is cut off by the panel edge the sheet is wrong. Plain soft grey-green studio backdrop in every panel, even soft daylight, no scenery, no captions or labels.

Subject: ONE visiting monarch, alone on the sheet: the King of Clubs, a man about 60 years old, a real human actor. Broad and dignified, about 180 cm tall. Grey hair and a full grey beard; grey eyes; composed, courtly, slightly bored expression. His dress follows the group rule, quoted verbatim from the costume bible: 'visiting 1862 playing-card monarchs in their own suit colours: the King and Queen of Clubs in black and ivory, the King and Queen of Diamonds in scarlet and gold, the King and Queen of Spades in black and slate grey, each robe cut as a stiff flat rectangular card panel bearing its suit symbol and edged with ermine, over 1862 court dress, crinoline gowns for the queens and knee breeches with tail coats for the kings, gilt openwork crowns and small coronets each with its suit symbol at the front, the backs of the robes in a crimson-and-cream lattice card-back pattern with a small heart rosette; stately and rich'. On this one king that means: black and ivory only; a stiff flat rectangular ivory card-panel robe edged with ermine, bearing large black club symbols; beneath it a black 1862 court tail coat and black knee breeches with ivory stockings; a gilt openwork crown with a club symbol at the front. No heart symbol anywhere on the front.

Style: Photorealistic live-action fantasy film rooted in England in 1862, shot on 35mm film with anamorphic lenses, 16:9 widescreen. Real sets, real locations and real costumed actors in 1862 dress. Wonderland spaces are real built sets and set extensions in an Alphonse Mucha-inspired Art Nouveau design: flowing organic lines, floral and vine ornament, circular halo roundels, mosaic and stained glass, aged pastel-and-gold surfaces with patina and moss; the waking 1862 meadow stays plain period realism. Talking animals and fantastical creatures are photoreal CGI animals with naturalistic anatomy, real fur, feathers, skin and scales, lit by the same light and grounded with real contact shadows. Natural and practical light: sunlight, candlelight and oil lamps, soft haze with volumetric light shafts and soft colour through stained glass. Restrained palette of verdigris teal, slate grey, dusty rose, soft sage and lilac pastels and tarnished-gold accents, warmed by amber sun and candle glow. Fine film grain, gentle halation, soft depth of field, grounded and quietly melancholy.

Layout recap (highest priority): four separate panels side by side, exactly one king in each panel, the same man in front / side / back full-body views and one head-and-shoulders close-up; no queen, no other figures.
